sites.rationale: L7 names Gly-378 explicitly as the SNAP-tag insertion point; Python confirms seq[378]='G' and seq[379]='T', both topology O (extracellular). The site is 40 residues from the TM boundary (TM starts at 418), comfortably satisfying the ≥3-residue rule. L4 independently names the same Gly-378 junction for a 16-aa insertion with preserved activation, and L6 generalises that the juxtamembrane region tolerates such insertions. Full-length DDR1b was engineered with a SNAP tag inserted after Gly-378 in the extracellular juxtamembrane region (DDR1-SNAP construct); the membrane-anchored receptor was expressed in cells and labeled on the surface with cell-impermeant SNAP substrates.

sources.claim: The DDR1-SNAP construct encoded DDR1b in which the SNAP tag is inserted after glycine-378.

sites.rationale: [Literature audit 2026-11-05 (deliverome-analysis PR 236), verdict confirmed_exact: position confirmed at this residue. validation_level surface_and_function -> function_only (paper reports surface: not_reported, function: yes). Paper (PMID 24671415): "insertion mutant DDR1-GS2. A 15-amino acid sequence was inserted after Ser-397.". Audit note: Human DDR1b (Q08345 canonical, 913 aa) in a C287S background; S397|L398 matches. Collagen-induced autophosphorylation of GS2 was normal (Fig 7). No direct surface assay for GS2: surface arrival is inferred only from the mature glycoform band (deletion mutants' surface trafficking is 'data not shown'), so surface_and_function is overstated to function_only.] L5 names Ser-397 explicitly; Python confirms seq[397]='S' and seq[398]='L', both topology O (extracellular). The site is 21 residues from the TM boundary (TM starts at 418), satisfying the ≥3-residue rule. L6 provides additional general support that the juxtamembrane region tolerates insertions without disrupting activation. The 15-aa insert is within the ~13–23 aa range of a short epitope tag. A 15-amino-acid flexible segment was inserted after Ser-397 in the extracellular juxtamembrane region of full-length DDR1; the paper reports this insertion was tolerated with no adverse effect on receptor activation.

sources.claim: A 15-amino acid sequence was inserted after Ser-397.

sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface display confirmed by anti-FLAG immunostaining; collagen I-induced ectodomain shedding assay performed with DDR1-NF, demonstrating the tagged receptor is functional and responds to ligand stimulation.
sites.rationale: L1 names the junction explicitly as between Lys-23 and Gly-24; Python confirms seq[23]='K' and seq[24]='G', both within the extracellular domain (EC 19–417 per landmarks). The insert site is 5 residues into the mature ectodomain (SP ends at 18), well clear of the SP cleavage site and far from the TM boundary (395 residues). L2, L3, L8, and L9 all corroborate surface display of the same N-terminal FLAG construct. Full-length DDR1 constructs (DDR1-NF and DDR1-NHA-CF) were engineered by overlap-extension PCR with FLAG or HA epitopes inserted between Lys-23 and Gly-24, three amino acids downstream of the signal-peptide cleavage site; constructs were transiently expressed in HEK293 cells and confirmed to display the tag on the cell surface.

sources.claim: N-terminal FLAG or HA epitopes were inserted three amino acids downstream of the signal peptide cleavage site (between Lys-23 and Gly-24), and the C-terminal FLAG epitope was introduced before the stop codon.
